shortTitle: Diaphragm Pacing by Phrenic Nerve Stimulation
fullTitle: Diaphragm Pacing by Phrenic Nerve Stimulation
apaCitation: Perez, I. A., Kun, S., & Keens, T. G. (2016). Diaphragm pacing by phrenic nerve stimulation [Patient education handout]. American Thoracic Society.
bestFor: Recognition and patient-education context for diaphragm pacing in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome/high cervical spinal cord injury, device components, candidacy concepts, alternate ventilatory support, oximetry/CO2 monitoring, risks, equipment failure, body-position effects, and upper-airway obstruction during pacing.
authorityBoundary: Patient-education and therapy-recognition support only. Specialty physician evaluation determines candidacy; current manufacturer/specialty-center instructions, physician orders, facility policy, and current monitoring guidance govern device use and response. Current AASM scoring rules govern any PSG respiratory-event scoring. This therapy must not be conflated with transvenous phrenic-nerve stimulation used for selected adults with central sleep apnea.
therapyIdentityBoundary: Diaphragm pacing for ventilatory support in conditions such as CCHS or high cervical spinal cord injury is a distinct therapy from transvenous phrenic-nerve stimulation for adult central sleep apnea.
copyrightUse: Use bibliographic metadata, section labels, page locators, and original Sleep Pathways Guild teaching directions only. Do not reproduce the handout's protected graphics or substantial prose.
